Document.project_name: Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HI-CAS) -Bhutan
Document.proponent: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD)
Document.description: The Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya Region (HI-CAS) is a regional project implemented in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and implemented by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) in partnership with the Tarayana Foundation in Bhutan. The project aims to improve climate-resilient, nature-positive livelihoods while strengthening the leadership and agency of rural women and Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs). The project will deliver locally tailored climate adaptation solutions that are grounded in feminist and human rights-based methodologies thus ensuring an inclusive approach that place the rights, agency, and leadership of IPLCs at the centre. These evidence-informed Integrated Adaptation Solution Packages (IASPs) will combine springshed management, renewable energy technologies for power irrigation systems, and agrobiodiversity practices. They will be complemented by capacity building and knowledge sharing to drive institutional policy and action and to attract sustainable investments in climate action and development, particularly in the water, energy, and agrobiodiversity sectors, with a strong focus on the leadership of women and IPLCs.

Document.project_name: Regional Assessment of the St. Lawrence River Area
Document.description: A Regional Assessment of the St. Lawrence River Area will be conducted to better understand the potential effects of past, present and future developments. The Impact Assessment Agency of Canada and Indigenous partners are jointly leading the Regional Assessment, and will provide opportunities for Indigenous communities and organizations, non-governmental and governmental organizations and the public to participate in a meaningful way to determine appropriate activities, outcomes and boundaries. Document.project_name: Fortress of Louisbourg des Roches Parking Lot
location: Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site is seeking to develop a new visitor entrance location at the current bus loop accessed through Gate 1 at the end of Park Service Road on the Barachois. Project components will include the construction of a new parking lot in the location of the current bus loop and des Roches building (Fisherman's House), relocating the des Roches building to a new foundation (outside of the new parking lot footprint), relocating the outbuilding to serve as a kiosk and point of entry, and relocating the on-site fish flakes. The existing septic tank will be relocated to the new kiosk location within a heavily disturbed area and the kiosk itself will utilize existing utilities via conduit. Work will be conducted with heavy machinery from within the proposed new parking lot footprint.

Document.project_name: Fire Pump and Generator Replacement at John Weir Foote Armoury
location: John Weir Foote Armoury, 200 James Street North in Hamilton
Document.description:
The existing fire pump and associated emergency generator at John Weir Foote (JWF) Armoury is near the end of its service life. As part of the on-going operation and maintenance for the JWF Armoury, both of these systems are scheduled for replacement.

The fire pump head has been assessed and was determined to be oversized. The rationale for the oversized fire pump is attributed to the recent James Street North underground infrastructure upgrade carried out by the municipality, which increased the municipal water supply pressure to the Armoury. As part of the life cycle upgrade, the associated system of galvanized steel pipes for the fire pump will also be replaced. The proposed new fire pump is a vertical in-line fire pump package with jockey pump, flow test bypass and controller.

The emergency generator is approximately 27 years old with 240 hours run time recorded. Though a well maintained and regularly exercised generator can have a service life between 10,000-15,000 hours, age is a contributing factor which impacts the equipment's life cycle. The engine exhaust stack is deteriorated beyond repair and requires replacement. Several code deficiencies were also identified for the generator fuel oil storage and supply system. Based on the age, condition and code deficiencies, the emergency generator is planned for replacement. The proposed generator replacement will include a built-in double wall base tank, muffler, sound enclosure and a new engine exhaust stack.

Document.project_name: Accommodations and Classroom Upgrades - Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs
location: Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) proposes a project. The Canadian Armed Forces Training Area (CAFTA) Cedar Springs is an active training facility located on the edge of Lake Erie in Cedar Springs, Ontario. This range and training facility runs approximately 70 training events per year with the expectation that this number will increase in the coming years. As such, the existing CAFTA Cedar Springs accommodations and classroom buildings are lacking the infrastructure to support the expected increase in training events at this Site. DND intends to increase the available space for accommodation of personnel, both through renovation of the existing accommodations building and construction of a new accommodation building for further capacity, to be more consistent with the proposed future capabilities. The project will provide more classroom space to accommodate the anticipated larger numbers, ultimately increasing the capacity and availability of the range and training area (RTA) to Units.

Renovation of the existing accommodations facility will result in accommodations for up to 120 people, while construction of a new classroom facility is expected to accommodate up to 60 people. Additional project activities to take place will include pedestrian traffic control and road upgrades, fire alarm systems with integration between existing and new facilities, and the installation of a new septic tank system to replace the existing septic with new piping connected to infrastructure for the classroom and accommodations facilities.

Document.project_name: Edith Cavell Road KM 1.6 Slope Stabilization
Document.description: Parks Canada is proposing slope stabilization work along Edith Cavell Road in Jasper National Park, at a location where the existing slope stabilization measure, an interlocking concrete block retaining wall, is beginning to fail due to increased erosion of the slope above following vegetation loss during the 2024 Jasper Wildfire. A site-specific, targeted approach will be used to address the area of instability, including slope flattening and the installation of an engineered control measure at the base of the slope along the roadway. The project is intended to reduce the hazard, protect the roadway, and support safe travel.

Document.project_name: HMCS Hunter Embankment Erosion Repair
location: HMCS Hunter, 90 Mill Street in Windsor
Document.description:
The outer limits of the harbour are protected by a harbour wall of varying construction, along the northern and eastern limits. The southern limit (approximately 100 metres) however, is only partially protected (approximately 70 metres) by an armour stone wall. The remaining portion of the southern limit (the southeast corner) consists of an outcrop of land made-up primarily of what appears to be rock and soil that has, over time, been subject to erosion resulting in the need to have the area protected to prevent the further erosion and impact to the neighboring property.

In addition, erosion has been observed on a small peninsula on the northern boundary of the harbour near the exit to the Detroit River This erosion appears to have caused significant damage to the embankment in that area and now poses a potential threat to infrastructure (sidewalk and light-standard) near the shoreline.

The remaining outcrop is dredgeate from the historical construction activities and thus will be characterized to ensure suitable management. Furthermore, mitigation measures will be developed and implemented in order to protect potentially impacted SAR species and habitat (i.e. Northern Madtom).

Document.project_name: Pond (reservoir) dredging and replacement of the shutoff valves of the fire suppression network supply system.
location: Canada Border Services Agency Training Facility
Document.description:
The pond located on the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) College (hereinafter referred to as the "College") property, located at 475 Grande-Ligne Road in Rigaud, was created in the early 1980s to serve as a water supply for the campus's private fire protection system.

Over the years, a layer of sediment has accumulated on the bottom of the pond, jeopardizing the proper operation of the inflow shut-off valves and fire pumps that supply the system. BSA has retained BGIS, through Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), to dredge the pond and replace the shut-off valves of the inflow the main line.

The work will include the staging of a work area and sediment dewatering area, sediment dredging, dewatering and management of dredged materials, beneficial reuse or disposal of the dredged materials depending on their physicochemical quality, and the replacement of the shut-off valves upstream to the pumping station.

Document.project_name: Space Weather Station – Gaspé QC
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) has proposed a project. DND intends to install four unoccupied Space Weather Stations consisting of one or more Transmit and/or Receive antennae, a small shelter in which to house the hardware, and a perimeter fence. They will form part of a network of such installations that will collectively measure real-time fluctuations in the ionosphere (i.e. space weather) in order to map it as a reflecting surface for high-frequency radio signals.

This information will be used as part of Canada's Arctic Over-The-Horizon Radar project.

Document.project_name: Grassy Narrows First Nation Family Services Building Construction
Document.description:
Grassy Narrows First Nation is proposing to build a new Office in the community for Kitapinoojiminaanik Family Services (KFS). The building will be a single story timber-framed structure approximately 1,487 squared meters with additional features including an exterior covered deck, fenced playground area, adjacent greenspace and a parking lot.
The design intends to be fully accessible, with office space for Administration, Prevention, and Protection services, and rooms for training, meetings, families, and cultural spaces. Lot service connections will be extended from existing water and wastewater lines as well as hydroelectricity and telecommunications. Other physical activities include clearing, grubbing, excavation of topsoil and backfilling for foundational requirements and one section of community road will be re-aligned to provide safer sightlines and right of way standards.
The project is well aligned with Grassy Narrows First Nation planning initiatives and goals of the community leadership, to provide support for children, youth, and families.

Document.project_name: T1Clean Heat Central Utility Plant Decarbonization Project – Geoexchange Test Boreholes
Document.description:
Proposed Project: T1Clean Heat Central Utility Plant Decarbonization Project – Geoexchange Test Boreholes

This project involves the following:

As part of the Greater Toronto Airports Authority's (GTAA's) Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program, GTAA is evaluating a geoexchange system to support the future decarbonization of heating and cooling systems at Toronto Pearson International Airport.

The proposed project consists of constructing and testing three geothermal test boreholes on developed federal airport lands in the vicinity of the Central Utility Plant at 3255 Elmbank Road, Mississauga, Ontario which consisting of paved surfaces, utility areas, and previously disturbed lands.

The test-borehole program will evaluate drilling feasibility, subsurface conditions, ground thermal properties, thermal performance, and the constructability of deep vertical and angled geothermal boreholes. The information obtained through the program will support the design and environmental evaluation of a potential future geoexchange borefield.  The test boreholes are intended to remain in place following testing and, if confirmed to be suitable, may be incorporated into the future geoexchange system.

Project activities are expected to include:


	Surveying and confirming the test-borehole locations
	Utility locating and preparation of the drilling work areas
	Mobilization and operation of geothermal drilling equipment
	Drilling one vertical and two angled test boreholes
	Installation of the polyethylene U-loops
	Bottom-up placement of thermally enhanced grout
	Pressure and flow testing of each installed U-loop
	Completion of a 48-hour thermal-conductivity test on each borehole
	Documentation of geological formations, groundwater conditions, drilling observations, and thermal-test results
	Management of drilling water, cuttings, and other drilling materials
	Demobilization and restoration of the affected work areas.


Several sustainability best practices will be incorporated into the projects design and implementation for the wider Toronto Pearson Airport Longterm Investment in Facilities & Terminals (LIFT) Program.

Document.project_name: Radio Observatory – 5762 Akins Road
Document.description:
The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Defence Research and Development Canada intends to install a radio observatory consisting of up to approximately 1,000 antennas, consisting of vertical metal poles of approximately 6 metres in height, spread over an area of up to 60 hectares. The antennas will be connected to a central control shelter by wires. The proposed site will also include security fencing to control access.

The radio observatory will be a receiving station that will be used to assess the direction-of-arrival of radio signals in the high frequency band, from transmit stations at other locations in Canada.

The radio observatory builds on capabilities demonstrated by previous similar large-scale high frequency receive arrays built at the same site, such as the sampled aperture receive array that was active at the site in the 1980s. The radio observatory will be receive-only and will not emit radio signals nor produce any radiofrequency hazards.

Soils Remediation – Garrison Petawawa
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. 4 Canadian Division Support Group (4 CDSG) Environment Services, Garrison Petawawa, is proposing the environmental-compliance driven remediation of contaminated soils in a graveled parking and vehicle/equipment storage compound directly south of 80 Montgomery Road (Building BB-130). Soils characterized as exceeding applicable Federal soil quality guidelines will be removed from the site to a licensed receiving facility.

Document.project_name: LaPointe Pier Repairs - GCT Vanterm
Document.description:
Legacy Environmental on behalf of Global Container Terminals Inc. proposes to conduct maintenance and structural rehabilitation of the LaPointe Pier located at GCT Vanterm in Burrard Inlet, Vancouver. The works are required to address localized failure and ongoing corrosion of sheet piles along the pier, including approximately 40 metres of collapsed sheet piles that have reduced berth depth and compromised structural integrity. The objective is to restore berth functionality, maintain safe operations, and stabilize existing infrastructure without expanding the footprint of the pier.

Proposed in-water works include removal of collapsed sheet piles from the seabed, installation of approximately 75 square metres of gabion baskets along the western pier face, and placement of approximately 490 square metres of riprap at the northeast corner of the structure. Additional activities may include re-securing existing sheet piles with anchor rods and steel strapping, installation of corrosion protection anodes, and underwater welding and drilling associated with these repairs.

Construction will be undertaken using divers working from the pier and/or a barge-mounted crane, with supporting equipment such as hydraulic tools, welding equipment, and material placement from barge or land-based staging. Works will proceed in phases including demolition/removal, inspection, installation of stabilization measures, and armouring. In-water works are anticipated to occur over approximately 10 weeks.

Document.project_name: Confederation Park Storm Sewer Renewal
St. Peter's Canal Emergency-Use Slipway Installation
Document.proponent: Municipality of the County of Richmond
location: St. Peters Canal National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The Municipality of the County of Richmond, on behalf of the St. Peter's Volunteer Fire Department (SPVFD), is proposing to construct a slipway at St. Peter's Canal National Historic Site, in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia. The slipway will be located on the Atlantic Ocean side of the canal, to provide a safe and reliable location for launching an approximately 18–20 ft emergency rescue Zodiac vessel. The construction will consist of the installation of five precast concrete slabs, each measuring approximately 3.1 m by 3.7 m, and the placement of additional armour stone as required. Excavation and grading will be required to prepare the site and support installation of the precast concrete slabs. The proposed works will be completed using heavy equipment, including an excavator, operating from above the ordinary high-water mark. A locked gate will be installed to restrict access to authorized emergency responders. Public access will not be permitted for the slipway. The slipway will improve reliable emergency access to the water and help reduce response times for water rescue and other emergency incidents.

Document.project_name: Amunitions Base and Ammunition Compound Street Lighting – CFB Suffield
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. DND at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Suffield is to execute a project to rewire and replace existing street lighting in the Base Admin area, and to install streetlights in the Ammunition Compound. Existing streetlight poles in the Base Administration area will be demolished. New pole-mounted LED streetlights and new 25 kV compatible underground wiring will be installed in both the Administration area and Ammunition compound. Directional drilling will be used to install wire conduits under roads and trenching will be used otherwise. Lights will be tied to existing electrical transformers.

Document.project_name: Town of Banff 26DP34 134 Muskrat Street Addition of Detached Garage
Document.description: The homeowner of 134 Muskrat Street has proposed a new detached garage at the rear of the property on an existing gravel parking area. The garage will have a 12-inch-thick slab-on-grade foundation. Its approximate dimensions will be 22 x 18 ft and 11 ft tall.

Document.project_name: Integrated Solid Waste Management System: Landfill Development Project for York Landing, Manitoba
location: Integrated Solid Waste Management System: Landfill Development Project for York Landing, Manitoba
Document.description:
York Factory First Nation (YFFN) proposes to design, construct, and operate an Integrated Solid Waste Management System anchored by a new engineered landfill facility for York Landing, Manitoba. The project will replace the aging and non-compliant waste disposal system and will support current and planned housing growth

The project will be delivered through final planning and capital construction phases. Final planning activities include environmental and geotechnical studies, Indigenous and community engagement, detailed road and landfill construction (IFC) design, and a decommissioning/remediation plan for the existing waste site. Capital work includes site clearing and grading, excavation, access road upgrades/extension, internal roads, landfill cells, leachate collection and lined retention pond, secondary treatment, drainage and surface water controls, passive landfill gas management/methane flaring, waste diversion areas, hazardous waste and e-waste/material sorting storage, organic waste composting, perimeter fencing/security, site signage, solar-powered infrastructure, an operations/storage/inspection building, and a transmission vehicle.

The new facility will include engineered cells with geosynthetic liners and drainage layers, a leachate collection network designed to protect groundwater, and landfill gas controls to reduce methane and odour. The project also includes closure, decommissioning and remediation planning for the existing waste site with long-term groundwater and environmental monitoring. The estimated construction footprint includes approximately 45,000 m2 of vegetation clearing, 15,000 m2 of excavation, and approximately 25,000 m2 of new construction/works.

Document.project_name: CC295 Aircraft Tie-Down Point Installation North Apron Adjacent to Hangar 9 (Spots 26 and 27) - 8 Wing Canadian Forces Base Trenton
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. DND proposes to install fourteen (14) permanent aircraft tie-down anchors to support two CC295 Fixed Wing Search and Rescue (FWSAR) aircraft parking positions on the North Apron adjacent to Hangar 9 at 8 Wing Canadian Forces Base Trenton. The project includes survey layout, concrete coring, localized excavation within the existing apron structure, installation of reinforcing steel and tie-down anchor assemblies, concrete placement and finishing, site cleanup, demobilization, and final as-built surveying. The activity will occur entirely within an existing developed concrete aircraft apron and is intended to provide aircraft restraint during high wind events.

Document.project_name: Laurentia Project: Port of Quebec Deep-Water Wharf - Beauport Sector
location: Port of Quebec Beauport Sector (North Shore)
Document.description: The Quebec Port Authority is proposing to extend the line of the existing wharf eastward by 610 metres in order to operate a deep-water terminal dedicated to containerized general cargo. The 31.7-hectare project would include the construction of a new berth and a retaining dike that would allow for the development of an additional 17 hectares of backshore space. The project also includes the construction of rail lines and road accesses, the reconfiguration of two outfalls and Henri-Bourassa Boulevard with the addition of an overpass, as well as the reconfiguration of part of the Port of Quebec's existing land for truck loading and the relocation of part of the recreation and tourism area for the development of the operations support area and the storage of empty containers.

Document.project_name: Lucky Man Cree Nation Cultural Centre and Site Servicing
Document.description:
Lucky Man Cree Nation  is proposing to build a new cultural centre, including a traditional knowledge sharing space, a future ceremony building, and associated pathways and access road. The project is intended to provide cultural spaces and amenities, as well as the required water and sewer systems to accompany these spaces. To service the building, a site servicing plan has also been developed, including a septic field (pipes), water cistern, trenches, and septic tank.

Site prep will include minor vegetation clearing and grubbing, as well as excavation and earthworks (grading). Construction will include excavation and drilling for the septic field, and construction (above-ground) of the traditional knowledge sharing space. Landscaping, re-seeding, and tree planting will also be completed surrounding the knowledge sharing space.

Document.project_name: Fisher River Cree Nation (FRCN) On-Reserve Permanent Diking
Erosion Protection Project
City of Kingston, New Public Boat Launch Installation on Colonel By Lake
location: Rideau Canal National Historic Site of Canada
Document.description: The City of Kingston is proposing to install a new public boat launch on Colonel By Lake within Cecil Graham Park. The dimensions of the proposed pre-cast concrete boat launch are 8 m wide x 23 m long and the location is situated within a natural bay (Esther March Bay). The total in-water footprint is expected to be ~416m2. Additional in-water site alteration plans include a new 3 x 22 m floating dock. Additional upland site alteration plans include a 3 x 2 m concrete headwall to support an access ramp to the dock, a shoreline path, picnic area, parking lot and driveway.

Document.project_name: Haley Brook Crossing Replacement
Document.description: The Haley Brook Crossing Replacement project is proposed to address the long-term deterioration of the existing twin culvert crossing located along Shepody Road within Fundy National Park. In the fall of 2024, significant erosion was identified between the two culverts, compromising approximately 40% of their length and creating a void in the road surface measuring approximately 1.2m by 1.0m by 0.6m. Emergency stabilization measures, including the placement of sandbags and riprap, were implemented to reduce erosion and maintain roadway safety. While these temporary measures have proven effective in preventing further deterioration, they do not provide a sustainable long-term solution, and ongoing erosion remains a concern. The proposed project is to replace the existing failing twin culvert crossing with a single open bottom arch culvert that will provide a safe, resilient, and reliable crossing for park operations, visitors, and the public. The replacement structure will restore stream stability and accommodate natural hydrological processes while reducing the risk of future infrastructure failures and associated maintenance requirements.

Document.project_name: Site Remediation at Heart's Content SCH, NL
Document.proponent: Fisheries and Oceans Canada – Real Property and Environmental Management (DFO-RPEM)
location: Heart's Content SCH is located in Heart's Content, Newfoundland (NL). Located in the southern Avalon Peninsula
Document.description: Install a soil/gravel cap over the upland portion of the site to eliminate the exposure pathway of contaminants that have been identified in soil at the site. The primary contaminant is PAHs. The cap will consist of an engineered, structural pavement ready pad consisting of a geomembrane liner, proof rolled rockfill subgrade and granular subbase and base layers, and possibly grass cover over a portion of the site. The installation of the cap will also include measures to prevent coastal erosion (e.g., heavy rock).

Document.project_name: Road Paving Program, various locations, Prince Edward Island National Park
location: Prince Edward Island National Park of Canada
Document.description: Parks Canada is proposing improvement works on roadways, parking lot and associated infrastructures within Prince Edward Island National Park: Wild Rose Lane, Dalvay Crescent, Ross Lane, Ross Lane beach access and Cavendish Grove access. The project will include reparation of pavement on paved road, new pavement on gravel road, road widening and development of new access road. The project scope also includes reparation of pavement on parking lot, parking lot extension/migration and the replacement/installation of culvert. Work will be conducted with heavy equipment from within the road and parking lot footprint.

Document.project_name: On-Farm Composting System, Pilot Project
Document.description: This pilot project proposes the establishment of an on farm composting system to help address orchard waste management challenges. Project will reduce landfill hauling requirements, and improve sustainability and nutrient cycling on-farm. Project will involve the installation of approximately 200 meters of electric fence and gate, as well as approximately 200 meters of underground pipeline to distribute water to the area from an existing source.

Document.project_name: Sorel-Tracy Port Terminal Project
Document.description: QSL International Ltd. is proposing the construction and operation of a new port terminal in the industrial-port zone of Sorel-Tracy, Quebec. As proposed, the Sorel-Tracy Port Terminal Project would include a new floating wharf and related intermodal infrastructures. The project would support the handling of bulk materials, such as fertilizer and road salt, as well as general cargo, such as oversized steel parts, and would accommodate approximately 35 ships per year.

Document.project_name: Sumas Multiplex
Document.description:
This project will build a new, culturally relevant, multi-purpose community and recreation facility (approx. 18,740 sq.ft [~1741 m2]) for the Sumas First Nation community, serving on-reserve residents and open to the general public. The facility will include a community hall/gymnasium, boardroom, hydrotherapy room, large kitchen, fitness centre, and pedestrian bridge over the neighbouring creek.

Based on the location (a former Brick plant land = ~16, 918 m2), a new design concept is being developed to accommodate the building infrastructure. The project location is within the boundaries of the Upper Sumas No 6 Reserve lands.


	Large site area (~6.59 acres)
	Increased capacity
	
		~18,000 ft2 multiplex facility
		~12,000 ft2 office space
		~240 parking spaces
		Over 1 acre of open green space
		Future expansion are (~1.34 acres)
	
	


Works for this project are also associated with Registry posting 80963 - relating to the remediation of the the old Brick plant on the site.

Document.project_name: Recreational dock dredging - 5345 Indian River Drive
Document.proponent: upland owner at 5345 Indian River Dr.
location: Recreational dock dredging - 5345 Indian River Drive
Document.description:
The proposed project

The project includes dredging of up to 2-metres of accumulated sediment around a recreational dock at the above noted property to prevent structural damage. The sediment accumulated during a late-2024 weather event which caused debris to flow down an adjacent stream and fill in the area around the project site's recreational dock.

The works include mobilizing a long-reach excavator to the foreshore, digging along the impacted side of the dock, and removing up to 1,000-cubic metres of sediment. The sediment would be placed upland, off port jurisdiction, for reuse in landscaping or upland disposal pending approval from the District of North Vancouver.

An Environmental Monitor will be on site during the works to ensure no impacts to fish or marine mammals, and to conduct turbidity monitoring of the exclusion zone. Sediment controls will be in place if deemed necessary.

The excavator will be upland in the dry, and works will take place during low tide only. No other in-water works are proposed, and no works related to the recreational dock are included in this application. The proposed project will take place within the least-risk fisheries window of August 16 - February 28 and will take 2-5 days to complete.

Document.project_name: Construct Modular Office Complex, Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Edmonton, AB
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Edmonton will be receiving 2000+ additional troops over the coming years and there is a deficit of office space, which will need to be met in spring of 2027. Infrastructure required to accommodate the 250-personnel modular office space has an estimated total gross interior floor area of 6,000 m2 and an exterior space of 9,000 m2 for parking and storage. The site is currently landscaped and mowed regularly during the growing season so there's no habitat for species at risk.

Document.project_name: Army Training Centre – Central (ATC-C) Meaford Staff Accommodation (M-202) Upgrades
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing a project. Real Property Operations proposes renovating Building M-202, located at Army Training Centre – Central (ATC-C) Meaford to address deficiencies and to allow for continued use of this facility. The project will include mechanical upgrades, such as removal of old boiler and installation of new boiler, heat pump and split Air Conditioning units, architectural upgrades, such as exterior repairs, new interior flooring, painting, new countertops and attic hatches, as well as electrical upgrades, such as new light fixtures, fire alarms, Carbon dioxide (CO2) detectors, and new electrical panel. Lastly, the proposed project will include the excavation of a trench for the installation of an underground electrical feeder line measuring approximately 125m in length which will be connected to building M-203. Any excess fill will be managed in accordance with federal and provincial requirements, with an intent to re-use in the trenches.

Document.project_name: Pump Station Demolition- 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
location: 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
Document.description:
There is a small, unused pumphouse on Department of National Defence (DND) land owned by Greater Vernon Water Utility. The pump house is 5.5 m x 8 m in size and is surrounded by a chain-link fence, which will also be removed. The entire project area including access from the nearby paved area is approximately 200 m². A hazardous material assessment was completed, and these materials will be removed prior to the pump house structure being demolished. The fence posts will be pulled from the ground without additional digging.

BC. Real Property Operations Unit Pacific det Chilliwack is carrying out an assessment and Species at Risk permitting in order to support the North Okanagan Regional District, who will carry out the demolition.

Document.project_name: Main Camp Utilities Upgrade at Vernon Military Camp
Document.description:
A Utilities upgrade project for the Vernon Military Camp (Main Camp) is planned to start construction in spring 2025.

The work will involve the excavation and disposal of existing underground utility lines, installation of new water, sewer and storm lines, installation of a backbone communication duct system, restoration of roads, grading, repaving and revegetating impacts areas within the Main Camp of Vernon Military Camp. In addition to the work occurring at the Main Camp, an existing concrete chamber on the west side of Okanagan Highway 97 will have the valves permanently closed, the abandoned meter removed and disposed of, the chamber cut down to a minimum of 1.0 m below grade, backfilled and abandoned. Both of these areas where work will be occurring are cumulatively referred to as the "Main Camp Project Area".

Document.project_name: Terminated: Pump Station Demolition - 3rd Canadian Division Support Group (CDSG), Detachment British Columbia Mainland - Chilliwack
Document.description: The Department of National Defence (DND) is proposing to remove a number of facilities over time. The Regional District of North Okanagan (RDNO) owns the Greater Vernon Water Utility (GVWU), and a number of these facilities are no longer in use. As a result, funding has been created to remove these facilities over time. The DND pump station is a small building located on DND land just off highway 97 when entering Vernon from the South. A demolition contractor has been secured for the work and plans to remove the small building (5.5m by 8m). The Project is approximately a 2 to 3 day project. The prime contractor will mobilize on site, review unexploded explosive ordnance (UXO) protocols with Notra, remove hazardous materials prior to demolition. Once the site is cleared of UXO and hazardous materials contractor will remove the building and chain link fence and legally dispose of non-recyclable materials.

Document.project_name: Department of National Defence (DND) NORAD A-OTHR (Arctic Over the Horizon Radar) Project at Military Aeronautical Communications System (MACS) Carrying Place
Buffalo River Dene Nation Stage 5 Subdivision
location: BUFFALO RIVER DENE NATION RESERVE NO. 193
Document.description:
The Buffalo River Dene Nation is proposing to construct a new subdivision to meet the community's need for current and future housing units. The proposed Stage 5 subdivision will provide up to 50 new lots and will occupy approximately 15 hectares of forested land. New infrastructure required as part of the subdivision includes high density polyethylene (HDPE) water main pipeline, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sewer main pipeline and manholes, water and sewer service lines, hydrants, roadways and drainage culverts, power and phone utilities.

Clearing and grubbing of the site is proposed to occur in the fall or winter to avoid the risk of harming migratory nesting birds. The extent of vegetation clearing will be kept to the minimum amount necessary to construct the new subdivision and to provide a fire break. Activities during construction include primary earthworks, new utility installation, sub grade construction, ditch construction, grading and landscaping.

Document.project_name: Deep Bay Parking & Pedestrian Access
location: Riding Mountain National Park of Canada
Document.description: Project Objective: During busy periods, the demand to access Deep Bay by vehicle, bike and foot traffic is more than what the existing infrastructure can accommodate. The parking lot can become hazardous for visitors due to overcrowding of vehicles and the inability of Wasagaming Drive to safely accommodate two-way traffic and parking. Project description includes creating a new gravel parking lot on the south side of TaWaPit Drive (can accommodate 38 vehicles) in a previously disturbed area, with a pedestrian access corridor and road crossing from the parking lot to the Deep Bay Area. Construction of the new parking lot and access corridor will require removal of vegetation and top organic layer, followed by placement of granular fill. Signage and highway painting will complete this phase. Following construction activities, Wasagaming Drive from the West Intersection with TaWaPit to the existing parking area will be closed to vehicular traffic, open only to bikes and pedestrians. Another pedestrian crossing will be painted where the new east ramp of the Lakeshore Trail intersects with this section of Wasagaming Drive.

Document.project_name: Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project
location: East Brandon Industrial Area within the City of Brandon
Document.description: Manitoba Hydro is proposing the expansion of an existing natural gas-fueled electricity generating facility, located in Brandon, Manitoba. As proposed, the Brandon Dispatchable Capacity Project would include the development of three new simple-cycle combustion turbines, with an anticipated increase in production capacity of approximately 750 megawatts. Project components would also include a 32-kilometre natural gas pipeline, two electrical transmission lines totalling 3.5 kilometres, and upgrades to the existing electrical transmission station. The project is expected to operate for about 30 years.
